newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian shares climb as turnover grows - FEB 13.
newsitem.headline: Latvian shares climb as turnover grows - FEB 13.

text.p: Latvian shares mostly advanced further on Thursday and overall market turnover grew slightly, dealers said.
Market volume was 142,000 lats and the Rietumu Bank market index added just 0.03 percent to 151.50. Saules Bank's Saule10 index climbed 0.21 percent to 153.12, below its January peak.
"The relative sluggishness will not be over until all key companies have handed in their 1996 balance sheets, which might take another month," Saules Bank head of equities Karlis Krastinsh said.
"Foreign investors are also lying low, expecting results," he added.
Daugavpils Chain was the most traded stock on turnover of 22,500 shares as it remained stable at 2.25 lats.
On the official list, usual market leader Unibanka edged up a notch to 3.25 from 3.24 lats trading 2,400 shares.
Riga Transport Fleet traded 9,100 shares and was also stable at 1.70 lats and Staburadze advanced two santimes to 2.55 lats as it traded 4,600 shares.

Elsewhere on the secondary list, Roja fish cannery saw its price fall 35 santimes as it registered activity of 900 shares while Mangali Shipyard added five santimes to 1.10 lats on volume of 9,900 shares.
The Lode Brick company remained stable at 2.06 lats on turnover of 4,800 shares and Jekabpils sugar traded 6,300 shares and fell to 0.62 santimes from 0.69 santimes.
The Veldze soft drink manufacturer was also active on turnover of 3,500 shares and climbed four santimes to 0.65 santimes.
